stem: Disaster management Authority

note: The chapter has no section called 'Nature of disaster management'. Its nearest heading is 'Nature and scope of disaster' (printed p112), which gives the six-phase list and the three aspects important for common citizens; the definition of disaster management itself is on p113-114. The answer is built from both and says so.

stem: Mock drill
Disaster Management Act, 2005
note: The chapter says only three things about the Act: that it 'has been passed in our country' (p115), that the structure of the Disaster Management Authority is introduced in the same paragraph, and that the National Disaster Response Force 'has been established as per the Disaster management Act, 2005' (p116). It gives no date of enactment and no section detail, so the answer is limited to those three and states the limit.

note: The chapter's 'Types of Disasters' chart (printed p110) does NOT list famine under any of its six branches. Famine is named as a natural disaster in the chapter's opening paragraph ('floods, wet and dry famine, cyclones, earthquakes, volcanoes') and again in the long-duration list on p109. The answer places it by that prose plus the chart's Atmospheric branch, which does list drought, and says plainly that the chart does not name it.

stem: Theft
note: The chapter's 'Types of Disasters' chart does not list theft either. Outside this question itself, theft appears in the chapter exactly once, in the word list of Exercise Q1. The answer places it under Man Made by the chart's own definition of that branch and says the chart does not name it.

stem: Some symbols are given below. Explain those symbols. Which disasters may occur if those symbols are ignored?
note: The nine symbols are printed as an unlabelled 3x3 grid of red-bordered diamond pictograms directly under the stem (printed p120); they carry NO text at all, so the row is unanswerable without the figure and one is attached. These are NOT the same symbols as the chapter's own fig. 10.2 on printed p116, which shows three DIFFERENT placards that do carry printed labels (FLAMMABLE LIQUID 3, FLAMMABLE GAS 2, EXPLOSIVES 1). The chapter never names or explains any of the nine.
